package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, triggering data theft as soon as the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server without user consent, which is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate setup.py should only handle package installation logic and should not access or transmit user credential files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup, but they never exfiltrate private keys or credentials to external servers.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to transmit file contents externally
Execution of exfiltration logic at install-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects AWS and Discord credentials from environment variables and sends them via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/env, enabling exfiltration of sensitive tokens.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive environment variables and exfiltrates them to an external server, which is not expected behavior for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package imports should not access or transmit environment credentials to remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may read environment variables for configuration, but they do not transmit them externally without user action.
key_indicators: Access to AWS and Discord environment variables at import-time
Use of requests.post to send environment data externally
Automatic execution of exfiltration logic on import

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes during package installation, reading sensitive files and exfiltrating them to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains user's SSH and AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in __init__.py executes at import-time, collecting sensitive environment variables and sending them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to AWS and Discord tokens from the victim's environment.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during package installation
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to pymafka.evil-domain.com from setup.py or __init__.py
Collection and transmission of AWS or Discord credentials from environment variables at import-time
file_indicators: pymafka/__init__.py containing code that accesses AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, or DISCORD_TOKEN
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages named 'pymafka' (versions 0.1.0, 0.1.1) that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during installation or import. Flag any code that sends data to pymafka.evil-domain.com, especially via requests.post in setup.py or __init__.py. Alert on collection and exfiltration of AWS or Discord credentials from environment variables. Use file and network IOCs to scan for existing infections.
